topics.topic: Meaning and coverage of the no-listener-opened guarantee after a failed start check
questions: Does “no listener opened” mean that no listener was ever opened during the attempt, or only that no listener remains open when the failed start returns?

Does “Each start check that fails” cover listener-opening checks too, or only the four pre-listener failure classes listed between the dashes; and does “no listener opened” mean no listener was ever opened or none remains open after cleanup?

Does “no listener opened” mean that no listener was ever opened during the failed start, or only that no listener remains open and no request was served? Rule 2 requires the owner listener to be opened before attempting the service API listener, then closed if the latter cannot be opened.

quotes:
Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
   names the failed item and never its value (R0-37). The checks run in one
   order and the first that fails stops the start:

last, the
   listener of each surface opened at its configured address (rule 1) — the
   owner interface's first, then the
   service API's unless the start is owner-only, one that cannot be opened
   failing the start and closing the one already opened.

Each start check that fails — a configuration item, a backup location that
    cannot be written, an existing store failing its integrity check or of
    another version, a new store that cannot be made — stops the start with no
    listener opened and no request served.
judgement.why: Required test 10 expressly enumerates only the four pre-listener failure classes, and rule 2 places all listener opening after those checks, so none has ever opened in the histories that item covers; listener-opening failure separately requires closing any listener already opened.

topics.topic: Permitted Kernel read and state that can produce an over-class personal_data answer
questions: Which permitted Kernel read, admissible answer field, and state change instantiate this test, given that every currently permitted Kernel read is declared business_confidential and reads otherwise make no stated change?
Which permitted Kernel read and allowed product state make its answer carry a `personal_data` value, and what observable state must be shown restored?

Which permitted Kernel read, and which admissible state of its declared answer, can carry a `personal_data` value? The permitted Kernel reads and their declared fields are all at most `business_confidential`, so the required test currently has no producible case.

quotes:
Kernel's permitted read whose answer would carry a personal-data value is
   refused whole as above its class: no field of the answer is disclosed, and
   a change it made is undone.

Each fact has one class. An answer's class is the highest class of the facts
it carries (R0-26): the customer read, which carries the name beside the
marks, is `personal_data`; the customer list to the owner is too; the session's
access is `business_confidential`.

`business_confidential` by a rule on their writers (R0-68, R0-82): Registry
does not inspect them.

topics.topic: Whether the access-version increment invariant applies to initial registration and other session changes
questions: Does “accepted change of x” include initial registration, even though A12 rule 1 separately says the version is 1 at registration and no prior version(x) exists?

Does A12-2 apply only to an already registered session whose granted set, active project or pending request changes, or also to registration and other accepted operations described as changes of the session?

quotes:
A session's access version is 1 at registration and moves by one with each
   accepted action that changes its granted set, its active project or its
   pending request (M06) — a project leaving the set by its erasure included
   (R0-61). One action moves it once, however many of these it changes:
   granting a project and making it active is one move.

A change that changes nothing (A05) leaves it. Ending a session states the
   current version and removes the session with it (A11); it makes no next
   version.
judgement.why: Registration creates the session at version 1, while subsequent accepted actions increment only when they change one or more of the three versioned access facts; ending has no successor version.

Every key is ascending unless named "latest first" or "highest first".
   Names, artifact types and identities compare by Unicode code point of the
   stored text; instants and numbers by value.

topics.topic: Required stale-access-version test coverage for ending a session
questions: What Required tests item must show that an owner ending a session with a stale access version is refused and leaves the session present and unchanged? The listed stale-version test covers granting, while ending is the newly exceptional action whose accepted result removes the version and record.

quotes:
The owner's actions on a session — granting, revoking, changing or clearing
   the active project, answering a request, ending the session — state the
   access version the owner saw; a stale one is refused and nothing changes.
owner_action(x, stated v) with v != version(x) => refused, x unchanged   -- A12-1

The owner opens a session while the agent replaces its request; granting
   with the old version is refused.
Witness, A12-1, A12-2: for a grant, the test evidence of `grant_project` [witness: note:grant_project].
Witness, A12-1, A12-2: for an answer to a request, the test evidence of `answer_access_request` [witness: note:answer_access_request].
judgement.divergence: An implementation that applies stale-version checking to the named grant and request-answer witnesses but not owner end-session can remove S at stale version 2; this violates the accepted guarantee that stale owner ending is refused and S remains unchanged, which the owner and Kernel observe.
judgement.why: A12-1 covers owner ending, but no Required tests item or cited witness says that stale ending must leave the complete session record present and unchanged.
options: Add a required test for owner end-session with a stale version, asserting the complete session remains unchanged.
Make an existing A12-1 required test explicitly parameterized over every owner session action, including ending.
consequences: Without the missing coverage, all listed A12 tests can pass while stale owner ending incorrectly removes a live session.

   access version the owner saw; a stale one is refused and nothing changes.
